order: Make the engine's protocol server honor a cancellation notice instead of discarding it. Today a stopped call keeps running, because the runner blocks inside a synchronous spawn and cannot act on a signal, and the engine beneath it is a grandchild the server never tracked, so a call the operator believes stopped goes on editing the working tree unattended. Keep a registry of in-flight runs keyed by request id, and on cancellation tear down the whole process tree, using the tree-killing utility on Windows and a process-group terminate followed by a kill elsewhere. Answer the cancelled request with an explicit warning that the working tree may be half-finished and unaudited. Guard against loose id matching, so that only an exact id can reach a run and a spent numeric id cannot alias onto a live string id and stop an unrelated one, and drain every in-flight run at teardown, so nothing this server started outlives it.
claims: Done. Cancellation notices are now honored end to end. An in-flight registry ties each request id to the run it started, and a cancelled run has its whole process tree taken down, by the tree-killing utility on Windows and by a process-group signal pair elsewhere. The reply to the cancelled request states plainly that the working tree may be half-finished and unaudited. Id matching is guarded so a spent id cannot reach a live run, and teardown drains whatever is still in flight. Verified by running node tests/mcp-lane.test.js, which reports OK with 68 passed.
